text: In one English town, squares are painted on the street with names: places people paid for. Jesus paid for your place of favour.
explanation:
In an old English town with a famous yearly parade, squares are painted along the streets, each with a name inside: people who've bought the right to stand there on the day. Nobody pays for a spot and then stays home, satisfied that their name is on it. They come and stand in it.

"Having been justified by faith, we have peace with God… through whom also we have access by faith into this grace in which we stand." Jesus paid for your square on favour ground, and your name is written on it. Don't just know it; possess it. Say, "I'm standing on favour ground. When trouble comes, God turns it around for my good."

text: At the cross, noon became midnight: Christ in a circle of darkness. At the resurrection, He stands in a circle of light, and you're in Him.
explanation:
At His birth, angels filled the night sky so that midnight was like midday. At the cross it was the reverse: "It was about the sixth hour, and there was darkness over all the earth." Picture Christ at the centre of a circle of darkness, bearing every sin, every curse, every judgment that was ours.

Then picture Him risen, at the centre of a circle of light, under God's unclouded favour, without our sins, which were left behind in the tomb. And God "raised us up together." No one imagines Jesus is out of favour with God today. "As He is, so are we in this world."

text: Elisha told the king to strike the ground with the arrows of deliverance. He struck only three times, and won only three victories.
explanation:
On his deathbed, Elisha had King Joash shoot "the arrow of the Lord's deliverance," then said, "Take the arrows… strike the ground." The king struck three times and stopped. "The man of God was angry with him, and said, 'You should have struck five or six times; then you would have struck Syria till you had destroyed it! But now you will strike Syria only three times.'"

Israel "limited the Holy One of Israel." We do the same when we ask small and expect little. God "is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think." If the arrows are His deliverance, keep striking.

text: God doesn't just answer prayer. He over-answers it.
explanation:
As a young man, standing on a staircase in a block of flats, Joseph Prince asked the Lord for a wife from Him, and added, "Make her pretty as well." He says God gave him far more than he asked for.

That's how God gives. Jesus fed five thousand with five loaves and two fish, and twelve baskets were left over. His supply always exceeds the need. Often it's we who refuse, like a friend who insists on paying the bill and robs the giver of his joy. Let Him bless you. Only after you've received from Him can you truly give.

text: Paul wanted "the righteousness which is from God by faith," so "that I may know Him and the power of His resurrection."
explanation:
"That I may be found in Him, not having my own righteousness, which is from the law, but that which is through faith in Christ… that I may know Him and the power of His resurrection." Notice the order. Knowing God intimately, and experiencing His resurrection power, flow from being settled in righteousness as a gift.

The new covenant promises, "They all shall know Me, from the least of them to the greatest… for I will forgive their iniquity." That's why people with no church background can come to know God so deeply once they grasp they're forgiven. Declare it daily: "I am the righteousness of God in Christ." The more you do, the more you'll know Him.

text: God made Christ "head over all things to the church." The church isn't as poor as a church mouse. It's the body of the One who reigns.
explanation:
God raised Christ "far above all principality and power and might and dominion, and every name that is named… and put all things under His feet, and gave Him to be head over all things to the church, which is His body." Jesus is head over all things for your benefit. Whatever you're facing has a name, and you're seated in Him far above it.

The world calls the church a dull building for old people, "poor as a church mouse." But the church is the body of the One who said, "All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth." Things that loom over you are, in God's eyes, under your feet.
